/storm-damage/.description: Wind, hail or ice damage? Panda Exteriors offers free storm-damage roof inspections, meets your insurance adjuster and helps you through the claim, from the first photo to your new roof.

hero.title: Storm damage? We’ll help you through the claim
hero.sub: Most homeowners insurance policies cover sudden, storm-related roof damage. We inspect your roof for free, meet your adjuster and handle the roofing side of your claim, from the first photo to the final shingle.

form.title: Free Storm Inspection
form.text: We check your roof, gutters and attic, and photograph everything.

sections.title: Storm Just Hit? Do This First
items: Put safety first
Stay off the roof and away from downed lines or sagging ceilings. Ladders and wet shingles don’t mix.
Take photos and videos
Photograph the roof from the ground, the yard, gutters, siding and any leaks inside, with the date. It helps your claim.
Look for hidden damage inside
Check ceilings and the attic for stains, drips or damp insulation. Not all damage shows from the outside.
Call us as soon as possible
We inspect and document the damage, and can add temporary protection, like a tarp, to stop more water getting in.
link: What to do in the first 24 hours

sections.title: Will Insurance Pay for Your Roof?
sections.intro: Your policy decides, but storm damage insurance usually works like this:

sections.title: Your roofing advocate, not a public adjuster.
sections.text: You stay in control of your claim and talk to your insurance company; we bring the roofing facts, photos and a detailed estimate. Your insurance company decides what is covered, and sometimes the best advice is not to file at all.

sections.title: Storm Damage Questions, Answered
items: Will my insurance pay for a new roof?

Often, when the damage is sudden and storm-related: wind, hail, falling limbs or the weight of snow and ice. Old age and wear and tear usually aren’t covered. Your deductible and your type of coverage affect what you pay.
How long do I have to file a claim?

There is no single deadline. It depends on your policy, your state and the type of claim, and many policies require prompt notice. The safest approach is to have the roof inspected and notify your insurance company as soon as you know about possible storm damage.
Should I file a claim before getting an inspection?

You don’t necessarily need to. An inspection can show whether there is storm damage and whether it is likely to exceed your deductible. But don’t let it delay reporting serious damage, like a tree on the roof or water coming in.
What’s the difference between ACV and RCV coverage?

Actual cash value (ACV) pays for the roof’s depreciated value, so an older roof gets a smaller payout. Replacement cost value (RCV) is meant to pay for a new roof of similar kind and quality: often an ACV payment first, then the withheld depreciation once the roof is replaced. You pay the deductible either way.
What if more damage is found during the replacement?

Removing shingles can uncover damaged decking, underlayment or flashing. It should be reported as soon as it’s found; we document it and help submit a supplement to your insurance company for the extra work.
What if my claim was denied or underpaid?

A denial or lowball offer doesn’t always have to be the final word. A second-opinion inspection, with a detailed photo report and a line-item estimate, can be used to ask your insurance company for a reinspection or a supplement.

sections.title: Solar Options, Answered
items: What’s the difference between solar panels and solar shingles?

Solar panels are mounted on racks on top of your existing roof. GAF solar shingles are the roof itself: they lie flush with the rest of the roof and make power, installed as part of a new roof. We install both and will help you choose.
Do I need a new roof to go solar?

Not for solar panels: they are added to the roof you already have. GAF Timberline Solar shingles are installed as part of a full roof replacement, which makes them a cost-effective choice when your roof is nearing the end of its life.
Which makes more power?

Panels make a little more power per square foot and can be angled toward the sun, which helps on smaller or partly shaded roofs. Solar shingles need more roof area for the same output, so they suit medium to large roofs with open sun.
Which costs less?

Solar panels generally have a lower upfront cost per watt installed. Solar shingles cost more at first because they are a new roof and solar in one, and offer greater long-term value when you are replacing an aging roof anyway.
How do they hold up in storms?
Both are built to withstand the elements. GAF solar shingles are designed to handle wind, rain, hail and snow, and can withstand winds up to 130 MPH.
Can I finance my solar project?

Yes. There are various options, including solar loans, leases and power purchase agreements. Talk to us about the best option for you at your free estimate, and ask about $1,500 off your solar project.
